openQuestions: server/app.py's generic POST .../ops endpoint accepts ANY registered Op by name (not just text edits) and returns its jsonable result -- confirmed this covers InspectOp and RenderPageOp too (base64-encoded for the latter), so the web UI's Op-sending code path never needs a per-Op-type special case beyond the dedicated GET .../render convenience route

Found and fixed one real FastAPI + `from __future__ import annotations` bug this session: a dependency function defined as a closure inside an app-factory function is invisible to FastAPI's Annotated[X, Depends(f)] resolution (it evals the stringified annotation against the route's __globals__, where a local closure doesn't exist) and fails SILENTLY -- no startup error, routes just stop treating the parameter as a dependency. Every future FastAPI route in server/ must define its dependency functions at module level (see server/app.py's verify_token and _get_journal), never as a nested closure, even though the closure version looks like it should work and mypy/ruff won't catch it.

assets/fonts/ now has Bitstream Vera (Latin) and a Noto Sans CJK SC subset (Simplified Chinese); README.md's follow-up is widening the Latin set to a broader OFL family (Cyrillic, Greek) and possibly adding Traditional Chinese/Japanese/Korean CJK coverage

RTL scripts (Arabic, Hebrew) are not supported for editing: PyMuPDF applies contextual shaping before drawing, so texttrace reports shaped presentation-form glyphs, not logical characters -- a literal find/replace against logical RTL text will not match. Documented in tests/engine/test_font_cjk.py's module docstring; not attempted.
CJK vertical writing mode is not supported: Page.insert_font(..., wmode=1) did not produce vertical text through the API path tried. Also documented there, also not attempted.

fit=True (FNT-10) fragments a span's texttrace into one span per character, breaking a second edit's ability to find that text as one span -- documented as a known trade-off in engine/edit.py's replace_span_text docstring, defaults to False
FNT-09's kerning only reads legacy 'kern' tables, not GPOS pair positioning; no GSUB ligature substitution is attempted at all

font-name matching between texttrace and Page.get_fonts()/pikepdf now goes through engine.fonts.match.normalize_font_name plus a containment-match fallback in two places (engine/edit.py's _find_font_entry and engine/fonts/tounicode.py's recover_broken_spans) -- three real, distinct name-mismatch bugs were found this way across P2; reuse this same pattern rather than comparing font-name strings directly anywhere new

detect_blocks (engine/fonts/blocks.py) assumes its input span list is already in visual top-to-bottom order -- true for freshly-authored content but not guaranteed after an edit, since replace_span_text appends fresh draw operators to the end of the content stream. Not a bug for reflow_block's own use (it always computes the block from pre-edit spans), but worth knowing if UI-02/UI-04 ever re-run block detection on an already-edited page.

ReflowTextOp's overflow check runs before its require_tier check (engine/ops/text.py), so an overflowing edit is reported as overflow even when the real issue is also a weak font match -- both are surfaced eventually (allow_overflow=True lets the tier check run too), but the error message a caller sees first is whichever condition is checked first, not necessarily the most actionable one

Single-line alignment isn't detected: a replacement keeps the original span's LEFT edge, so shorter text in a right-aligned (or centered) line drifts off its alignment. Found on a real statement's right-aligned header. Detecting right/center alignment (e.g. from the span's position within its container or neighbouring lines) and anchoring the new text accordingly is a natural FNT-10/FNT-11 follow-up.

Metric-match confidence looks overcalibrated across families: Delta-Book -> Maiandra GD (MAIAN.TTF) and Roboto -> Trebuchet both scored 0.98 on a real document. Approval is still required at that tier, so nothing is applied silently, but the number overstates similarity.

CLI: a match string starting with '-' (e.g. '- End of Statement -') is parsed as an option by Click; users need `--` before the positional args. Documented in the test instructions; a CLI-level fix could accept it via an explicit --match option.
